takeaway: Gastric acid is stimulated by acetylcholine, gastrin from pyloric G-cells, and histamine from mast cells.

question.text: Gastric acid secretion is stimulated by which of the following?
question.say: Gastric acid secretion is stimulated by which of the following?

lines.text: The stomach is a furnace making gastric acid.
lines.say: The stomach is a furnace, and it makes gastric acid.

lines.text: The golden drops of acid are made by the parietal cells.
lines.say: The golden drops of acid are made by the parietal cells.
(laugh) Gastrin shouts through a megaphone: make more acid! It is produced by the pyloric G-cells.

lines.text: Histamine, from mast cells, stimulates the parietal cells directly.
lines.say: Histamine, produced by mast cells, stimulates the parietal cells directly, and boosts the effect of gastrin.

lines.text: Acetylcholine from the vagus nerve is the third.
lines.say: The third factor is acetylcholine, from the vagus nerve, which reaches the parietal cells directly.

lines.text: Remember: acetylcholine, gastrin and histamine stimulate acid.
lines.say: Remember: acetylcholine, gastrin, and histamine stimulate gastric acid.
